text.tspan: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing): what 10.0.1.0/24 really means
Network part: the first 24 bits are FIXED (that's what /24 means)
→ every address in this subnet starts with 10.0.1.
Usable for your servers and pods: 10.0.1.4 to 10.0.1.254 = 251 addresses
What was wrong in the drawing
1 · 10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24 were used in AZ a AND AZ c.
Subnets in one VPC can never overlap.
3 · The usable range was written as .1 – .255.
On AWS it is .4 – .254 (.255 is broadcast).
4 · 10.0.256.256 can't exist: each part is 8 bits, 0 – 255.
5 · /24 is too small for EKS pods: every pod takes a VPC IP.
Use /20 or bigger for app subnets.
